jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor in Causal inference jointly at the Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed and the Pioneer Center for AI
jobs.description:
A three-year position as Assistant Professor in causal inference jointly within The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed and The Pioneer Center for AI to be employed at the Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen. The position is available from 1 March 2027, with the exact start date to be agreed with the successful candidate.

About the Pioneer Centre for SMARTbiomed: The Pioneer Centre for Statistical and computational Methods for Advanced Research to Transform Biomedicine (SMARTBiomed) will support a critical mass of researchers who focus on method and software development for analysis and inference from massive human data, advancing applications in medicine. The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed will leverage large-scale, multimodal biomedical data combined with focused innovation in statistical and computational methods including machine learning to advance our understanding, treatment, and prevention of human disease. More information can be found here: https://smartbiomed.dk/

About the Pioneer Center for AI: The Pioneer Centre for Artificial Intelligence focuses on fundamental research, and within an interdisciplinary framework, develops platforms, methods, and practices addressing society’s greatest challenges. Hosted by the University of Copenhagen’s Department of Computer Science, cooperating institutions, Denmark’s Technical University, IT University of Copenhagen, Aalborg University, and Aarhus University co-lead the efforts along with Director, Professor Serge Belongie. More information on the center can be found here: https://www.aicentre.dk/ 

Information about the Department of Public Health can be found at: https://publichealth.ku.dk/

Job description
A successful candidate will conduct causal methods research at an international level. In the position, the candidate will work with both Erin Gabriel, (Causality theme lead and Co-director of SMARTbiomed and Professor at the Department of Public Health) and Sebastian Weichwald (Causality co-lead at the Pioneer Center AI and Associate professor at the Department of Mathematics) and aid in the supervision of a joint PhD student. The position is meant to be a bridge between the two centers, in causality, a theme both centers share. Specifically

The responsibilities will primarily consist of:

• 
Manage their own academic research and administrative activities

• 
Conduct research in line with the overlapping goals of the two pioneer centers in causal inference

• 
Contribute to evolving the research priorities of the two pioneer centers

• 
Support the collaborative infrastructure of the two pioneer centers

• 
Lead research papers pertaining to their own work and collaborate in the preparation of research publications. Ensure that software research outputs are provided to ensure maximum utility.

• 
Be a part of the supervision of the associated joint PhD student

• 
Develop ideas for new research projects

• 
Present papers at conferences and public meetings

• 
Take part in research-based teaching

• 
Supervise students, research assistants and postdocs outside of the joint student associated with the position

• 
Applying for funding for the next stage of their career

• 
Contribute to the administrative activities of both centers as needed

• 
Participation in formal pedagogical training programme for assistant professors

Profile
The successful applicant should have a PhD in Applied math, Statistics, Biostatistics, Computer science or a closely related area (e.g., pure mathematics with work in computational biology). The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

Assessment of applicants 
General criteria apply to the appointment of professors at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, innovation and societal impact, organizational contribution and leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement.

Find information about each criterion here: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/criteria-for-recognising-merit.

Place of employment
The Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen.

Terms of employment
The employment as Assistant Professor is a full-time and fixed-term position for 3 years. Starting date is 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible hereafter.

Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 39,993 DKK/approx. 5,349 EUR (August 2026 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.

Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025. 

Questions
For further information please contact Erin Gabriel by email: erin.gabriel@sund.ku.dk and Sebastian Weichwald email: sweichwald@math.ku.dk (using the subject prefix “[P41]”).

Foreign applicants may find this link useful: ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

Application procedure
Your application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format. Additional documents will not be considered as part of the evaluation.

• 
Cover letter (Max 1 page): Stating at which level you are applying, substantiate your qualification for the position and your motivations.

• 
Curriculum vitae (Max 3 pages): including education, research experience, other relevant skills

• 
Complete list of publications and preprints.
Highlight up to two publications that are particularly representative of your research. For each, provide no more than two sentences explaining its significance to you and the field, and your specific contribution. The selected publications need not be your most highly cited.

• 
Research plan (Max 3 pages): Description of current and future research plans

• 
Teaching portfolio (max 3 pages): outlining teaching experience and teaching plans

• 
Diplomas: Master and PhD degree or equivalent. If you do not yet have a PhD diploma, please just upload a PDF stating your (expected) PhD date.

Application deadline: 10 December 2026, 23.59pm CET 

We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the above mentioned requirements.

The further process
After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorised recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed, each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities. 

The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

Moment Professionals is recruiting on behalf of FPRT a Strategic Projects & Business Operations Manager based in Vojens, Denmark. We are looking for a project manager with a consultant's or project developer's mindset, who takes ownership of cross-functional business projects, takes the first step in understanding and structuring an issue and brings the CEO clear recommendations. The role suits you if you want to build structure in a company that is being built right now, with pragmatic, lightweight project management appropriate for a greenfield environment.

Your everyday at FPRT

You report to the CEO and take over the project management of FPRT's business and corporate projects, which the CHRO carries today alongside HR. The role has no direct reports to begin with, and you work across most of the company, with the Chief Production Officer, the process engineers, production, data, finance, HR and supply chain, as well as external implementation partners and advisers. The CEO communicates briefly and precisely, often on chat, takes challenge well and builds the collaboration on trust. Your mandate grows as that trust grows.

In the first months the SAP implementation is the largest task. An external partner implements the system, and you are FPRT's internal business project lead for the implementation: you keep track of progress and next steps, translate operational needs into clear requirements together with the functional owners and drive the solution into daily use across production planning, stock management, logistics and the integration of the systems FPRT selects in this period. Next come warehouse and logistics, selected governance and cross-functional operating processes, and business cases, for example for a new factory. Along the way you coordinate grant applications, public funding submissions and bank and investor material with internal owners and external partners.

You take the first step in understanding and structuring an issue, identify what information and expertise are needed, and then involve the right people. When a financing partner sends a long list of questions with a 48-hour deadline, you draft the answers from the documents that exist, mark how certain each answer is and bring them to the CEO and the right colleagues for a short validation. You prepare decisions as options, risks, advantages and price on one page with a clear recommendation, and you escalate delays and unresolved risks with a recommendation of your own.

The role is based in Vojens. You have the flexibility to work from home when a task needs focus, and in intense project periods you are on site every day, sometimes for a month or more. English is used a lot in daily work, and Danish is preferred, since FPRT is building a company in Denmark. If your Danish is not fluent yet, the right competencies count most.

And then there are the benefits:

A central role close to the CEO with direct influence on how a new company is built, ownership of business systems, processes, funding and business cases from day one, a mandate that grows with the trust you build, a culture where challenge with facts is welcome, and flexibility to work from home when focus requires it.

To succeed in the role…

…you do not need to have carried the title project manager or to come from defence. What matters is that you take ownership of cross-functional business projects, structure an issue before you involve the right people, and give a firm recommendation with the reasoning behind it. You also take pride in:

• 
challenging the CEO and colleagues with arguments and keeping the dialogue constructive.

• 
finding the information yourself and knowing when to escalate.

• 
keeping project management agile, with the minimum structure that makes it work.

• 
working with a risk until it is reduced, once you have identified it.

• 
involving busy colleagues firmly and kindly, so they like working with you.

What you need to bring:

• 
Either a relevant degree in business administration, finance, economics, engineering management or a related field, or equivalent experience, and at least five years of relevant experience or a strong track record of cross-functional business projects.

• 
Basic project management skills, including stakeholder management and risk assessment, gained through education or practice.

• 
Experience as business project lead or coordinator on an ERP or other business-system implementation. Method and implementation experience matter more than specialist system knowledge.

• 
Executive-level communication in English, written and spoken: short, clear and decision-oriented.

• 
The possibility to be on site in Vojens every day in intense periods.

It is an advantage if you:

• 
come from management consulting or advisory, for example an audit and advisory firm such as the Big 4, or from business transformation, corporate development or strategy and operations in a scale-up.

• 
have worked with grant applications, public funding, or bank and investor material.

• 
have prepared business cases and cost-benefit analyses for executive decisions.

• 
speak Danish.

Do you want to join the team at FPRT?

Moment Professionals manages the recruitment process on behalf of FPRT. We review applications continuously and close the process when the right candidate has been found.

The process may include interviews with Moment Professionals and FPRT, a case, relevant tests and reference checks.

Due to the sensitive defense-tech nature of FPRT's projects and operations, all potential employees are subject to a police and intelligence background check as part of FPRT's standard recruitment process. Continued employment is conditional upon obtaining and maintaining the necessary security clearance.

If you are interested, you are very welcome to apply via the application link, and we will assess your application as soon as possible. If you have questions that can help you decide whether the position is right for you, you are welcome to contact Moment Professionals by phone on +45 70 20 18 35 or by email at info@moment.dk. All enquiries are treated confidentially.

The company

FirePoint Rocket Technology (FPRT) is building one of the most unique and strategically important industrial projects in Denmark: a new production facility for solid rocket propellant and advanced defense-tech components. FPRT's ambition is significant: the company is scaling from the early operational phase to 300+ employees within the next 18 months. Joining FPRT now means becoming part of the core team shaping a new high-tech, safety-critical production environment from the ground up.

**Why we are hiring

**Spirii is growing. We work with charge point operators, businesses and fleets in several European markets, we take part in more and more tenders, and our commercial team has grown along the way. With growth comes friction. Deals and tenders are tracked in different places, the numbers in the CRM do not always match what we bill, and it takes too much effort to answer simple questions like “what will we close this quarter?”

We want one person to own the engine behind our revenue: the CRM, the data, and the path a customer takes from first contact to signed deal, onboarding and correct billing. That is this role. You will make work easier for our sales, marketing, onboarding and customer success teams, and you will give leadership numbers they can trust.

**The team

**You will report to our CSO. You will own Revenue Operations from end to end, and you will work every day with sales development, account executives, marketing, onboarding and customer success, and closely with Finance on billing data.

**What You Will Do

****CRM and tools

**

• Own and improve HubSpot, our CRM, so everyone works from the same clean data

• Make sure every deal and tender is tracked in one place, from first contact to result

• Set up and improve lead routing

• Bring in the other tools the commercial team needs, such as order management, bid management and lead development

• Make sure master data is correct, so billing runs smoothly

**Metrics and forecasting

**

• Define and track our core SaaS metrics: ARR, ACV, TCV, NRR and pipeline stages

• Run the weekly forecast and track how accurate it is

• Connect marketing, sales development, account executives and customer success, so the forecast reflects what is really happening

**Data and reporting

**

• Build dashboards that leadership trusts and uses to make decisions

• Keep the CRM clean and reconcile it with billing data

**Planning and sales process

**

• Build one clear sales process, with the same stages and rules from lead to handover across teams and markets

• Support territory design and regional planning reviews

• Run capacity modelling and lead quota planning

• Improve the path from lead to opportunity

**What Success Looks Like After Your First Year

**

• Leadership opens one dashboard and trusts what it sees

• Every deal and tender lives in HubSpot, and CRM data matches billing data

• The weekly forecast is a habit, and it gets more accurate over time

• Every market follows the same sales process

• Our sales team spends less time on admin and more time with customers

**What You Bring

**

• 5+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations or commercial analytics in a B2B SaaS company

• Strong CRM administration skills, ideally in HubSpot

• A track record of building tools and processes that help a sales organisation work better

• Comfort with data: Excel, SQL, or BI tools such as Tableau

• A good understanding of SaaS business models and unit economics

• Hands-on experience bringing AI tools into a sales or marketing team

• Fluent English. Another European language, such as German, French, Dutch, Swedish, Danish or Italian, is a big plus

• A degree in business, engineering or a similar field, or equivalent experience

**Who You Are

**

• You enjoy building things from the ground up, and you are comfortable when not everything is defined yet

• You take ownership and follow through

• You can think big picture and still roll up your sleeves to fix a workflow yourself

• You explain data clearly, whether you are talking to a sales rep or to the leadership team

• You like working with people from many countries and cultures

**Benefits

**It is important for us to create a healthy, diverse, fun, and creative working environment, so besides all the basic benefits, we also focus a lot on social activities, flexible working hours and a good work life balance.

• Flexible Work Environment: Enjoy a collaborative, inclusive, and open workplace designed to fit your needs and support work-life balance.

• Competitive Package: A competitive salary, an 11% company pension plan, and a comprehensive benefits package.

• Time to Recharge: Benefit from 32 paid vacation days and paid parental leave to focus on what matters most.

• Career Growth: Access professional development opportunities and grow your career in a high-impact, high-growth industry.

• Stay Energized: Enjoy excellent coffee, tea, free snacks, and subsidized lunches at the office.

• Stay Active: Use our Spirii gym and shared company car to keep moving.

• Make an Impact: Be part of a team driving the future of sustainable energy while working on meaningful projects.

The position is a permanent position in Copenhagen, Denmark. Danish language is not a requirement, but Fluent English language skills are required.

**About Spirii – Who We Are

**Spirii is a full-service e-mobility provider which offers hardware and software charging solutions to companies in the private and the public sector. Spirii was founded seven years ago as a company. Nevertheless, the people in Spirii have extensive experience working with electric cars and charging, as well as the development of future transport- and energy systems.

Spirii is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences. Spirii strives to create an inclusive and diverse workplace, and we encourage all qualified applicants to apply regardless of age, gender, race, sexual/religious orientation, or disability.

Please note: This is a full-time office-based role (5 days/week)

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Newbuilding Manager to take commercial ownership of complex newbuilding and vessel investment projects across their full lifecycle, from initial business case and market engagement through contracting, construction and delivery.

This is a senior commercial role requiring strong judgement, negotiation capability and the ability to navigate high-value, complex investment decisions in a global environment. You will work closely with Fleet Technology, Network Strategy, Chartering, Vessel Portfolio Management, Finance, Treasury, Legal and other key functions to ensure projects deliver the right balance of commercial value, contractual protection, technical requirements and long-term value.

Beyond individual newbuilding projects, you will provide senior commercial capacity across the wider tonnage agenda, supporting transactions such as sale and purchase (SnP), purchase options, sale and leaseback arrangements, newbuild for time charter and contract amendments.

Key responsibilities

• Drive the commercial development, procurement and execution of assigned newbuilding and vessel investment projects, from business case through tendering, contracting, construction and delivery.

• Lead or contribute to investment business cases covering vessel specification, timing, commercial structure, risk, CAPEX, cash flows and total cost of ownership.

• Lead or support shipyard engagements, tender processes, bid evaluations and negotiations of Letters of Intent (LOIs) and Shipbuilding Contracts, in close collaboration with Legal, Fleet Technology and Finance.

• Lead commercial yard due diligence and counterparty assessments, including financial strength, risk and compliance, together with Finance, Treasury and Compliance.

• Act as the commercial contract owner throughout the project lifecycle, managing contractual milestones, payments, guarantees, options, claims and amendments.

• Coordinate cross-functional project teams and ensure high-quality, timely governance submissions, decision papers and management reporting.

• Provide flexible senior commercial capacity across the wider tonnage portfolio during peak periods, including SnP transactions, purchase options, sale and leaseback projects, newbuild for time charter and contractual amendments.

• Monitor shipyard capacity, pricing, market dynamics and competitor activity, translating market intelligence into actionable commercial analysis and recommendations.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with key shipyards, shipbrokers, OEMs, advisers and internal stakeholders.

• Contribute to consistent commercial processes, knowledge sharing and lessons learned across the Newbuilding team.

• Work closely with fellow Senior Newbuilding Managers, providing support and project coverage as portfolio priorities and workloads evolve.

• Identify and escalate material commercial exposures and decisions outside agreed mandate to the Head of Newbuilding, while maintaining ownership and momentum of agreed workstreams through completion.

Who we are looking for

You are a commercially strong shipping professional who can combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution. You are comfortable taking ownership of significant commercial commitments, challenging assumptions and navigating complex negotiations involving multiple internal and external stakeholders.

You bring:

• Significant commercial experience within shipping, vessel investment, newbuilding, sale and purchase, or a comparable capital-intensive industry.

• Proven experience leading complex commercial negotiations and managing high-value contractual commitments within defined mandates.

• Strong commercial judgement and the ability to balance price, vessel specification, delivery schedule, contractual risk and long-term value.

• Experience developing investment cases and translating complex commercial considerations into clear recommendations for senior management.

• A strong track record in tendering and contracting, combined with a solid understanding of key financial indicators including CAPEX, cash flows and total cost of ownership.

• The ability to manage several complex projects simultaneously and respond effectively to changing priorities and periods of high workload.

• Strong stakeholder management skills and experience working across multiple functions in a global, matrix organisation.

• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to influence and engage confidently at senior levels.

• A good understanding of vessel specifications and maritime technology.

• Experience working with Asian shipyards is considered a strong advantage.

• A high degree of ownership, commercial integrity and attention to detail.

What success looks like

Success in this role will be measured through:

• Commercial value and contractual protection secured across assigned investments and projects.

• Quality and timeliness of investment recommendations, decision papers and governance submissions.

• Delivery within approved cost, schedule, mandate and contractual parameters.

• Effective management of commercial risks, options, milestones and contractual deadlines.

• Ability to flex across projects and transactions as portfolio priorities change.

• Strength and quality of relationships with strategic shipyards and contribution to the continued development of the shipyard supply base.

You will play an important role in ensuring that major vessel investments are commercially robust, well governed and positioned to create long-term value, while strengthening our ability to engage strategically with the global shipyard market.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral researcher in quantitative genetics and genomics with a focus on inbreeding depression and genetic diversity management
jobs.employer_name: Center for Kvantitativ Genetik og Genomforskning
jobs.description:
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) at Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for an exciting two-year postdoctoral position in the field of quantitative genetics and genomics applied to inbreeding management in livestock populations. The primary focus of this position is to investigate the genetic bases of inbreeding depression in dairy cattle.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two-year position starting on 1 April 2027, or as soon as possible. 

Job description
This is an opportunity to integrate a top research environment and contribute to advancing the state of the art in inbreeding management, while working within a collaborative project involving key industry partners.

The overarching objective of the project is to quantify the impact of inbreeding depression load on economically important traits in dairy cattle breeds and to investigate whether recessive variants contributing to inbreeding depression segregate in genomic regions experiencing rapid accumulation of inbreeding. Particular attention will be given to regions surrounding monogenetic traits (e.g. polled locus, milk caseins) which have been subjected to strong selection pressure in recent years.

You will apply state-of-the-art quantitative genetic and genomic modelling approaches to evaluate the effect of inbreeding depression on a broad range of production and functional traits recorded in dairy cattle populations. To support these analyses, you will have access to extensive databases containing phenotypic records routinely collected on farm, as well as large-scale pedigree and SNP genomic datasets currently used in genomic evaluations. High-density SNP genotyping and whole-genome sequence data will also be available to search for causal variants and more finely describe the genetic architecture of inbreeding depression in dairy cattle. Ultimately, the project aims to incorporate these findings into practical mating software readily available to dairy farmers. Therefore, these activities will be carried out in close collaboration with industry partners to ensure practical implementation in the field. 

Within this position, the successful candidate will also have the opportunity to contribute to other research projects related to genetic diversity management and quantitative trait modelling across other livestock species. 

Your profile
• A Ph.D. in Quantitative Genetics, Population Genetics or similar.
• Good programming skills (R, Python or Julia)
• Experience in the use of software to estimate variance components is a plus (e.g. DMU, BLUPF90 or similar) 
• A team player and a good communicator
• A good track record of publication in international peer-reviewed journals
• Fluent in English (written and spoken)
Who we are
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) is a major center for research and education in quantitative genetics and genomics at Aarhus University (http://www.qgg.au.dk/en). We conduct basic and applied research in animal, plant, and human genetics. Our focus areas include quantitative genetics, artificial intelligence applied to agriculture and medicine, population genetics, and integrative genomics. Research within QGG is characterized by a very close synergy between method development and application on practical problems across species, in collaboration with industry partners. QGG is an international research center with about 70 employees and visiting researchers from over 15 nations. QGG works in teams and strives for an excellent working environment, in which we value self-leadership, open communication, and commitment to diversity and inclusion.

What we offer
The successful candidate will be offered: 

• An interdisciplinary environment, in which the candidate will be able to exchange across disciplines and diverse applications (livestock, plants and biomedicine).
• An international research environment characterized by collaboration, professionalism, commitment to diversity and inclusion.
• Computational resources, including access to the GenomeDK high-performance computing cluster.
• A healthy work-life balance.
Place of work and area of employment 

The primary place of work is C. F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000, Aarhus C (Denmark).

Contact information
For further information, please contact Tenure-Track Assistant Professor Alban Bouquet, +45 2070 2677, alban.bouquet@qgg.au.dk
Associate Professor Zexi Cai, +45 8715 7928, zexi.cai@qgg.au.dk

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in causality and machine learning for treatment decisions, jointly at the Pioneer Centre for AI and the Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed

jobs.description:
Department of Mathematical Sciences, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen  The Department of Mathematical Sciences (MATH) invites applications for a PhD fellowship in causality and machine learning for treatment decisions. The fellowship is shared between the Pioneer Centre for AI and the Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed and is advertised at the Faculty of Science together with a three-year assistant professor position in causal inference at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences.

  The start date is 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible.  We are willing to accommodate the successful candidate’s situation, and the exact date is a matter of agreement.

  The setup: one project, two centres  You will be supervised by Sebastian Weichwald (Associate Professor at MATH, Copenhagen Causality Lab, and causality co-lead at the Pioneer Centre for AI) and Erin Gabriel (Professor at the Department of Public Health, causality theme lead and co-director of SMARTBiomed), and work closely with the assistant professor hired at Public Health also working jointly at the two centers, so that the link between the centres runs through daily work, not only meetings.

  Causal inference is a theme both centres share and approach from two sides. This position is for someone who wants both.

  About the centres: The Pioneer Centre for AI (https://www.aicentre.dk/), hosted by the Department of Computer Science with partners across Danish universities, does fundamental AI research. The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed (https://smartbiomed.dk/) develops statistical and computational methods for large-scale biomedical data to improve the treatment and prevention of disease.

  The project  In diabetes management, continuous glucose monitoring is a high-frequency biomarker that is often used in treatment decisions. Given the huge amount of information summaries must be used; differences in summaries can lead to different decisions from the same raw data.  Treatment and prevention decisions increasingly rest on high-dimensional or high-frequency patient data such as biomarkers, wearable-device streams, omics profiles and longitudinal health records. In practice these are reduced to scores, coarser summaries, learned representations or patient states before a decision is made. The project asks when such a reduced representation still supports choosing between interventions, what is lost when it does not, and how representations can be learned with the decision in mind. It starts with the decision and works backwards to the measurements, transformations and assumptions that decision needs. This project aims to answer some of these questions in general, and to provide specific solutions In diabetes management.

  Who are we looking for?  The key requirement is competence: a master’s-level background with a high level of mathematical and computational training, for example from studies in statistics, mathematics, computer science or a nearby field, and an interest in causal inference. You should be interested in biomedical applications, ideally with some prior exposure through a thesis, a project, an internship or a collaboration, and willing to talk to and learn from clinicians and biomedical researchers about the context in which the methods will be used. Programming skills and willingness to turn methods into reusable software are expected.

   

  About the department

  The department has about 50 permanent scientific staff members, around 60 PhD students and 35 postdocs. It has strong research groups in many areas of mathematics and active PhD, postdoc, and visitors’ programs. Our buildings are located in central Copenhagen next to the central park Fælledparken. Our website https://www.math.ku.dk/english provides more information about the department and the research conducted at the department https://www.math.ku.dk/english/research/. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment.

  The PhD programme

  Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelors´s degree.

   Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. statistics, mathematics, or computer science. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant with the help of the supervisor.

  Terms of appointment and payment according to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of the integrated programme

  To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of up to 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year. A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7.426 before tax.

  When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   Responsibilities and tasks:

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teach and carry out knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at internationally recognized journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project 	
• Take part in the activities of both Pioneer Centres and spend time in both research environments   We are looking for candidates with the following qualifications and experience:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project, in particular a strong foundation in probability, statistics and/or machine learning at advanced master’s level 	
• Interest in and some exposure to biomedical applications, and willingness to work with clinicians and biomedical researchers 	
• Evidence of research ability in any form: a master’s thesis, a project, an internship or open-source work counts as much as a preprint; prior publications are not required 	
• Programming skills and interest in producing reusable, open software 	
• A curious mind-set with a strong interest in Mathematics and its applications 	
• Good English skills   Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include:

   	
• Motivation letter (approximately 1.5 pages)
 	Propose your own angle on the project and argue how it fits the two groups and the wider network, including the Pioneer Centre for AI and SMARTBiomed. Tell us why this joint setup: what you expect from working across both groups that you would not get from either side alone or from an industrial machine learning lab, and how your background prepares you for it, including any experience with biomedical or other applied collaborations. 	
• Curriculum vitae (max. two pages) including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• About you (max. one page, in prose). Tell us about the thing you are most proud of. We do not mean grades or prizes, but something you made or worked out: a report that was never published, a tool, a result, a course or side project. Say what it is and why it matters to you. Use the rest of the page for anything else you want us to know: people you have worked with, circumstances we should take into account when reading your CV, or context that does not fit a CV. 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.   How we assess

  We shortlist on the written application as a whole, weighing motivation and fit with the joint setup, the mathematical and statistical foundation relevant to the project, evidence of research ability in any form, and interest in biomedical applications. Publications are neither required nor an assessment criterion, and we do not rank applicants by the reputation of their previous institution. Selected applicants are invited to interview. Interviews may span several conversations, e.g. a technical follow-up and a conversation with the leadership of both centres. As part of this we may ask you to give a short technical presentation on a topic of your choosing, or for a sample of your work. What matters to us there is whether we can discuss science together and how we would work with each other.

  When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

  Application deadline

  The deadline for applications is 5 January 2027, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process

  After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment (shortlisted) by a committee of unbiased experts. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  An assessment committee will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

   

  Questions

  For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the supervisors: Sebastian Weichwald (see https://sweichwald.de/#research-with-us) and Erin Gabriel (erin.gabriel@sund.ku.dk).

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills.

The ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively across functions.

A curious, proactive and solution-oriented mindset.

Strong skills in Excel and PowerPoint.

• 
Experience with Logility or a similar demand planning system, and/or Aptos or another allocation system.

Knowledge of Power BI, Power Query or QlikView is considered an advantage.

• 
Fluency in English.

jobs.description:
At the Faculty of Engineering and Science, AAU Energy, a position as PhD stipend is available within the general study program. The stipend is open for appointment from January 1st or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years.

Your work tasks    
The position is offered in relation to the research group "Hydrogen and Electro Fuels" and the PhD Student will be positioned to the section for “Thermal Engineering”.

Your competencies 
As a PhD student in modelling and experiments on PEM water electrolysis, you will work at the intersection of chemical and electrochemical reactor engineering, with a particular emphasis on electrolysis. The project focuses on testing proton exchange membrane electrolysis cells, characterising their electrochemical performance and developing detailed electrochemical cell models. You will design and carry out experiments on single cells, analyse electrochemical behaviour under different operating conditions and use the resulting data to build, calibrate and validate mechanistic models that describe transport, kinetics and degradation phenomena.

An important part of your work will be to investigate how PEM electrolysers perform when conventional materials are partially replaced by recycled ionomers and iridium. You will compare performance, stability and degradation patterns with and without recycled components and translate your findings into a deeper understanding of the underlying electrochemical mechanisms. In parallel, you will conduct techno‑economic assessments of PEM electrolysis systems, including related life cycle assessment studies, to evaluate how material choices, operating strategies and system design affect costs and environmental impacts over the full life cycle.

The PhD project is carried out in the context of the CYCLOPEM, EDSOES and CAPEX projects, which provide access to state‑of‑the‑art experimental facilities and collaboration with academic and industrial partners. You are expected to participate in project meetings and to present your results at international conferences and workshops. In addition, you will contribute to teaching activities within courses on chemical and electrochemical reactors and take part in the daily activities of the Hydrogen and Electro Fuels research group  at AAU Energy, including group meetings, seminars and joint publications.

The applicant must have a relevant professional and/or educational background within thermal, chemical and electrochemical engineering. Modelling of chemical and electrochemical reactor and LCA.

Qualification requirements
PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 872 of 6 October 2026 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Who we are
AAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean
and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners and other academic environments to address real‑world energy challenges.

The department is located in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg/Esbjerg campus. AAU Energy employs around 250 staff members at different career stages and from a broad range of national backgrounds. This creates an international and interdisciplinary research environment with many opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. English is widely used as the working language in research and teaching, which makes it straightforward for international colleagues to integrate.

We offer access to advanced laboratory and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international external partners. As a workplace we value a collegial and inclusive culture with room for professional discussion, initiative and mutual support in everyday life. New colleagues, whether they come from elsewhere in Denmark or from abroad, can draw on the university’s support services related to relocation, housing and practical matters.

You can read more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk

How to apply
Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position
• Curriculum Vitae (CV)
• Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades) 
• Project description (4-5 pages), that: describes the applicant’s initial thoughts and ideas related to the specific project applied for. This includes a brief state-of-the-art (including short list of references), a time schedule and how the applicant intends to shed light on the project objectives
• Other relevant documents
The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website. 

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. 

Do you have any questions?     
If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information  
Read more about our recruitment process here.

The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts.
Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Read more about The Doctoral School of Engineering and Science

Salary and terms of employment
The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement). 

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

Changes to this advert made on 13 November 2026:

  The heading of the position has been updated so it correspond correctly to the project and position.

  Two sections has been added:

  Mobility rule and Eligibility as Doctoral Candidate (DC)

  Under the section “The position” the acronym and number of the grant has been added (highlighted).

  And due to the changes the application deadline are extended with two weeks from the original application date on 22 November 2026. New deadline for applying is 6 December 2026.

  The Human Centered Computing Section at the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen invites applicants for a PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI.

  The start date is expected to be 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The position
 This doctoral position is part of REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network (REGULAIRE - Project 101312218) bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions.

  Project description
 The PhD student’s research is expected to conduct in-depth qualitative studies of how EU digital regulation (e.g., AIA, DSA) is technically and organisationally implemented in SMEs developing AI-related technologies. The goal is to map developers’ translation of regulatory guidance into product and service design and compares implementation strategies across sectors. This project offers a focused route into human-centred computing, sociotechnical research and the study of regulation in practice. You will join an international cohort, receive supervision across institutions and take part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment.

  The PhD student to be recruited in this call is expected to define their PhD project within the scope of the overall project and collaborate with the larger project team.

  Description of the scientific environment
 The position will be within the Human Centered Computing section (HCC). The Human Centered Computing section is a highly interdisciplinary group that conducts research within the areas of Human-Computer Interaction, Computer Supported Cooperative Work, Ubiquitous and Pervasive Computing, Digital Fabrication and related fields. Our section aspires to be a top research environment that bridges technology, theory, and empirical studies. The Human Centered Computing research environment at the University of Copenhagen is internationally leading, as evidenced by it’s ranking as second in Europe according to CSRankings. Further information about research at the Department is available here: https://di.ku.dk/english/research/ .

  This position will be co-supervised by Irina Shklovski (email: ias@di.ku.dk) and Naja Holten Møller (email: naja@di.ku.dk) at the University of Copenhagen in the Department of Computer Science, Human-Centered Computing section. The PhD will be conducted in collaboration with Joris Van Hoboken, Professor of Information Law, with special emphasis on Law and Digital Infrastructure at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Faculty of Law, University of Amsterdam

  Who are we looking for?

   	
• Applicants should hold a MSc degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Data Science, HCI, Critical Data Studies, STS, Law and Policy or a related field. 	
• Good written and oral English skills are a requirement. 	
• Previous scientific publications (if any) and relevant work experience is encouraged 	
• Applicants must be willing to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities   The ideal candidate would have an educational background or prior work experience in technology development, prior experience in qualitative research and fieldwork in organisations, and some understanding of European regulatory and policy concerns around AI systems.

  The PhD programme
 You can undertake the PhD programme as:

  A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish Master’s degree.

  Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme equivalent to a Danish Master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the position, i.e. HCI or CS. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Additional qualifications for the MSCA PhD 

  REGULAIRE is funded by the European Commission’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie programme and to be eligible for this funding you must meet the following criteria:

   	
• You must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to your recruitment; 	
• You must work on the project full-time.   Please ensure that this information is clear on your CV. Researchers can be of any nationality.

  Mobility rule
 The researcher must not have resided or carried out his/her/their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately before the recruitment date. Short stays as holidays and compulsory military service and/or Refugee Convention 1951 are disregarded.

  Eligibility as Doctoral Candidate (DC)
 The recruited DC must be doctoral candidate, i.e. not already in possession of a doctoral degree on the first day of employment. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but who have not yet formally been awarded the doctoral degree will not be considered eligible.
 
 Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as a PhD fellow is full time, on site in Copenhagen, and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific position formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme

   	
• Carry out a research project with increasing autonomy from your supervisors 	
• Collaborate with researchers both within the research group, and with external project partners 	
• Author scientific papers aimed at high-impact venues 	
• Participate in the research and training activities with the REGULAIRE network 	
• Disseminate research nationally and internationally 	
• Attend PhD courses on general skills development such as academic writing, as well as relevant specialised courses such as REGULAIRE summer and winter schools 	
• Conduct a change of scientific environment in the form of a secondment with a relevant standards organisation and an extended visit with one of the REGULAIRE academic partners 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD position 	
• Relevant educational background 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional activities 	
• Good written and oral English language skills   Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Cover Letter detailing your motivation and background for applying for this PhD position; 	
• Research Statement detailing your desired research focus and goals for the PhD studies within the scope of the specified position. The research statement should demonstrate your independent thinking by outlining a concrete research direction within technology governance you wish to explore, including: specific research questions you aim to address, preliminary ideas on methodological approaches you would employ, connections to existing literature, and the potential impact and applications; 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position; 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted; 	
• Publication list (if available); 	
• Names and contact details of three references.   Application deadline: 

  The deadline for applications is December 6 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by unbiased expert assessors. You will be notified about whether your application will be selected for assessment.

  The assessors will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessments. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in January.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact Irina Shklovski by email: ias@di.ku.dk.

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.
